title: arXiv AI — 28 October 2026: six notable recent papers, inferred ordering
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This ordering is inferred from checkable discovery and attention signals, cross-list relevance, public artifacts, and reported evaluation scope. Citation evidence is limited: the six selected new submissions each had 0 Semantic Scholar citations at the snapshot; the order is not a readership or download ranking.

sections.title: EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations
sections.abstract: The authors present an open embedding model that maps text, images, audio, video, and mixed inputs into one space, with a staged training curriculum and configurable modality and embedding footprints.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a new Pareto frontier across their multimodal embedding benchmark suite, often matching or exceeding specialist models and models several times larger.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported benchmark results are author-run; Google's model card notes that quality can vary across languages and that training-data coverage shapes performance.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three core AI category listings, public model card and release, Hacker News discussion, and ArXiv TLDR listing; 0 Semantic Scholar citations at the snapshot.

sections.title: TeamGym: A Gym for Team Decision-Making by AI Agents with Distributed Information
sections.abstract: TeamGym tests and trains language-model agents on decisions requiring teams to find and share pivotal information from legal, finance, medical, and software-engineering source material.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report average success-rate drops of 22.9 percentage points when pivotal facts are distributed across agents and a further 19.9 points when agents must retrieve those facts themselves; two policy-training experiments improve final-decision quality and coordination.
sections.unique_caveat: The evaluation covers 8 language models, 12 corpora, and two policy-training experiments; it does not establish that the same gaps hold across all team structures or domains.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: ArXiv TLDR weekly curation and separate technical discussion; concrete communication/retrieval gap evaluation across 8 models and 12 corpora; 0 Semantic Scholar citations at the snapshot.

sections.title: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis
sections.abstract: The authors introduce SynthAPI, a way to vary tool, task, and database diversity in synthetic agent environments, and fit a scaling law relating data composition to downstream tool-use performance.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that, at larger training budgets, more tool and database diversity and greater data complexity can improve generalization more than adding tasks alone, with results across four agent evaluations.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that SynthAPI omits user-in-the-loop interaction and long, semantically rich documents, and that the proposed scaling law has been validated on one data-generation pipeline rather than shown to transfer generally.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: ArXiv TLDR weekly selection and Harness Hub analysis; 458,752 tasks and 849 trained models; 0 Semantic Scholar citations at the snapshot.

sections.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
sections.abstract: Heads of Security adds learned per-head attention gates to separate trusted instructions from untrusted content, aiming to let models read hostile text without obeying it.
sections.claimed_contribution: On Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and GPT-OSS-20B, the authors report 10% attack success for RL-Hammer against HoS versus 97% and 85% against the two cited baselines, and report stronger resistance to an adaptive white-box attack at higher attacker compute.
sections.unique_caveat: Tests cover two open-weight model families; the authors note that the proposed explicit attention constraint does not directly apply to linear-attention architectures.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in machine learning and language; independent technical discussion shortly after submission; 0 Semantic Scholar citations at the snapshot.

sections.title: VideoLVR: Latent Visual Reasoning over Grounded Video Evidence
sections.abstract: VideoLVR interleaves text reasoning with latent visual evidence tokens derived from relevant video regions, and also trains a policy to select visual tokens alongside text actions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that visual-token prediction lets models revisit localized evidence without adding cropped frames to the context, improving results over their base models across five video benchmarks and two backbones.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors identify reliance on synthesized spatio-temporal grounding annotations as a limitation and suggest extending latent visual states beyond localized evidence.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in vision and AI; included in ArXiv TLDR weekly selection; five video benchmarks reported; 0 Semantic Scholar citations at the snapshot.

sections.title: Timestral
sections.abstract: Timestral is a four-size family of probabilistic time-series forecasting models that combines decoupled horizon forecasting, known-future covariates, and synthetic pretraining followed by mixed real/synthetic post-training.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that the 123M- and 209M-parameter models rank first and second across the metrics they report for GIFT-Eval, TIME, and fev-bench.
sections.unique_caveat: Pretraining is exclusively synthetic and the headline comparisons are tied to the authors' benchmark protocols; broader performance on real deployment workloads remains unestablished.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Secondary coverage and public model weights/inference code; the paper is not cross-listed into another core AI category; 0 Semantic Scholar citations at the snapshot.
